title: WPMS/1254/2020 of M/S DALIP SINGH ADHIKARI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1254 of 2020
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. I.P. Kohli, Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Advocate for
respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Mr. D.S. Patni, Senior Advocate
assisted by Mr. Siddhant Manral, Advocate
for respondent no. 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
Petitioner is a contractor registered
with Uttarakhand Public Works Department.
He responded to a Notice Inviting Tender
issued by Uttaranchal Rural Road
Development Agency (Respondent No.2),
which was published in newspaper on
25.01.2020.
It is the case of the petitioner that his
technical bid was declared to be responsive
by the Technical Evaluation Committee vide
order dated 08.05.2020. But, subsequently,
on a complaint made by a rival bidder, his
technical bid was declared to be non
responsive vide order dated 26.05.2020.
Since he was not heard while passing the
order dated 26.05.2020, therefore, the said
order was quashed in a writ petition filed by
the petitioner, which was decided on
23.06.2020 and liberty was granted to the
competent authority to pass a fresh order
after hearing him.
Pursuant to the judgment of this
Court, another order has been passed on
31.07.2020 and his technical bid has again
been declared to be non responsive on the
same ground as was taken earlier.

In the order impugned in this writ
petition, petitionerís technical bid has been
declared to be non responsive on the ground
that the registration certificate produced by
the petitioner is in variance with his
partnership deed, inasmuch as in the
partnership deed which has been uploaded
by the petitioner, there are four partners,
while in the registration certificate there are
only two partners, therefore, legal status of
petitionerís firm is not clear.
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel
for the petitioner submits that petitionerís
technical bid in respect of two other works
was rejected on the same ground that legal
status of petitioner is not clear and this
Court vide judgment dated 18.11.2020
rendered in WPMS No.677 of 2020 has held
that the ground taken for rejecting
petitionerís technical bid is unsustainable.
The judgment relied upon by the petitionerís
counsel has been brought on record as
annexure no.1 to the supplementary
affidavit.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for
respondent nos.2 and 3 and Mr. D.S. Patni,
learned senior counsel appearing for
respondent no.5, while admit that identical
question was decided in WPMS No.677 of
2020, but they submit that the present writ
petition cannot be decided in terms of the
aforesaid judgment as here contract has
been awarded.
Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel
for the petitioner however, submits that the
contract was awarded after filing of the writ
petition.
Since identical controversy has been
decided in the judgment dated 18.11.2020
rendered in WPMS No.677 of 2020,
therefore, judicial propriety demands that

this writ petition be also decided in terms of
the aforesaid judgment.
Accordingly, writ petition is allowed in
terms of the judgment dated 18.11.2020
rendered in WPMS No.677 of 2020. The
impugned order dated 31.07.2020 is
quashed and respondents are directed to
proceed in the matter in accordance with
law.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Aswal 07.12.2020
